messages:
maria: onboarding nebula-70k (long-context) int4 build to dedicated pool. quick smoke shows divergence after ~46k tokens. kv-cache looks shifted relative to positional indexing. anyone seen this pattern?

sam: can you paste the minimal repro + logs? which quant backend (fbgemm/ggml/our-int4)? :eyes:

maria: using our-int4 runtime (v0.21.1), quantization pipeline int4-v2, rotary RoPE scaling = automatic. repro command:```
./bench_run --model nebula-70k-int4 --prefill 50000 --stream false --seed 42 --log-level debug
```
Log excerpt:```
[DEBUG] prefill: tokens=50000
[INFO] step 46010: gen_token 0x1f4a
[WARN] kv_insert mismatch: kv_idx=46012 expected_idx=46011
[DEBUG] pos_scale=1.0000001192092896
```

josh: reminds: mismatch like that usually indicates rounding drift in pos-scale multiply when switching from fp16->int8/4 accum path. the pos indices can slip by 1 if the rolloff threshold crosses during accumulation. did you try forcing pos_scale=1.0?

maria: tried setting pos_scale override to 1.0 in runtime config - quick rerun:```
./bench_run --model nebula-70k-int4 --prefill 50000 --override pos_scale=1.0 --seed 42
```
Result: no kv_insert mismatch in same window. :party:

alesia: nice. what's the perf hit? any memory delta on the dedicated workers?

maria: rough numbers from 3-run median on a single p4d worker: latency +6% p50 on long-prefill scenarios, mem +0.25GB due to forcing fp16 path for pos-multipliers in some kernels. throughput unchanged for short requests.

sam: tradeoff seems reasonable for correctness. but we need a targeted unit test in the long-context harness that reproduces the index-shift, and a small kernel-level fix instead of global FP fallback. can we get a minimal C repro to show where rounding flips?

josh: I started a microkernel test this morning that simulates incremental pos-mul quantized accumulation. gist:```
for (i=0;i<N;i++) {
  float64 acc = 0;
  acc += roundf((pos_scale * (float)i) * quant_factor);
  // compare to baseline fp32 accumulation
}
```
When quant_factor is non-integer the rounding boundary crosses at different i for fp16 vs fp32, producing the off-by-one in index mapping.

maria: attached a short trace we captured (pasted below). bench-bot, can you add a perf job with a canary that uses pos_scale=1.0 and another with pos_scale=auto on the nebula-70k-int4 model and run 24h long-prefill workloads?

bench-bot: scheduled: nebula70k-posfix-canary -> pool:dedi-longctx-1 (48h), nebula70k-auto -> pool:dedi-longctx-1 (48h). results will post to /bench/nebula70k/pos_scale_ab_test. ETA 26h. :white_check_mark:

alesia: for remediation options: 1) force pos_scale=1.0 for long-context int4 until we have kernel fix, 2) implement integer-safe pos-mul accumulation with deterministic rounding, 3) special-case prefill path to use fp32 for pos-mul only. opinions?

sam: prefer option 2 long-term. patching kernels for deterministic rounding is better for perf. short-term 1 or 3 acceptable as canary. we should also add an eval that compares model outputs on a curated long-priming gold set to detect subtle semantic regressions when pos_scale changes.

maria: created GH ticket #ML-1427 with reproducer, logs, and A/B plan. I will push a small harness test to our longctx-eval suite that reproduces the off-by-one pattern and adds assertion on kv indices.

josh: ping me on the kernel patch, I can help implement deterministic rounding variants (using ties-to-even or explicit fixed-point accumulation).

maria: thanks — will follow up in the ticket. leaving notes: do not roll nebula-70k-int4 to prod until canary finishes. if canary shows correctness + perf ok, plan a controlled rollout with feature-flag pos_scale override.

sam: ack. thanks for fast triage.

maria: TL;DR: long-context int4 bringup hit pos-scale rounding causing kv-index drift around ~46k tokens; forcing pos_scale=1.0 removes drift but costs ~6% latency; bench-bot running A/B canary; ticket #ML-1427 created for kernel fix and longctx regression tests.
